title: Moltbook, the agent-only social network, left its database open to anyone
summary: Security researcher Jamieson O'Reilly found that Moltbook, a social network where OpenClaw-based AI agents post to one another, had left a Supabase table without row-level security, exposing every agent's private API key together with claim tokens, authentication codes and owner-association data, about 1.49 million records in all; 404 Media confirmed the exposed credentials let a third party take over an agent account. The database was taken down and a patched OpenClaw released, with users told to update and rotate any leaked tokens or keys; the report also notes a separate one-click remote code execution flaw in OpenClaw whose leaked tokens carried operator.admin and operator.approvals permissions that could disable pre-execution approval and move execution from a Docker container to the host.
verification_note: URL fetched on 2026-10-17; GIGAZINE page dated Feb 02, 2026 confirms the Supabase row-level-security misconfiguration, exposed agent API keys, claim tokens and owner data (about 1.49 million records), O'Reilly's discovery, 404 Media's takeover confirmation, the database takedown, the patched OpenClaw release and the key-rotation advice. The page does not state that posts act as prompts to other agents or that thousands of agents could have been injected; those candidate claims were dropped and the summary is limited to the page text.
